item.title: Historic Virginia school for Black children reopens as museum after $6.2m restoration
item.description: The historic Union Street School in Leesburg, Virginia has reopened as a museum and community centre. After a refurbishment costing around $6.2 million, the building now serves to educate about Black history. Initially established in 1884, it provided education to Black children during segregation until 1958. The new museum aims to preserve memories and share the stories of those associated with the school. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: ‘She was a monster’: the real Patricia Highsmith, by the people who knew her
item.description: A new film starring Helen Mirren explores the Ripley writer’s later years, but was she really so rude and eccentric? Editors and publishers who worked with her look back Publisher and bookseller Otto Penzler has loved Patricia Highsmith’s work all his life, but their first meeting was a washout. In 1984, she agreed to give a reading at The Mysterious Bookshop, his store on West 56th Street in New York. item.title: Reclaiming Mary Cassatt: putting overlooked American artist back at heart of impressionism
item.description: New exhibition restores painter’s place as leading figure in French movement that revolutionised art As a painter, friend, and collaborator of Edgar Degas, who exhibited with impressionist artists including Claude Monet and Camille Pissarro, Mary Cassatt was at the heart of the 19th-century movement that emerged in France and revolutionised art. She was also a woman and foreign – “American, American through and through” is how she described herself. As a result, in the 100 years since her death, Cassatt has been frequently overlooked in the country where she produced her best work. Continue… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.title: China TCM doctor defies medical secrecy by carving 100 private prescriptions on her tombstone
item.description: A tombstone for a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) doctor, engraved with 100 prescriptions she developed, has gone viral on mainland social media, with many people praising her generosity and noble character. The tombstone is in Xiping county, in central China’s Henan province. It commemorates Yuan Shufang, who practised TCM for eight decades and died in 2006 at the age of 97.
